conditional_thesis: Loop-based LLM agents are structurally justified for long-horizon, open-ended, partially observable, externally verifiable tasks because one-shot autoregressive decoding lacks task-utility search, external feedback, reliable revision, and state control.

research_questions.question: Does loop-based operation outperform one-shot decoding on long-horizon tasks?
research_questions.falsifiable_answer: Supported only if loop conditions beat one-shot baselines after cost reporting.

research_questions.question: Is external feedback necessary for loop benefits?
research_questions.falsifiable_answer: Supported if grounded tool/test/retrieval feedback beats self-reflection-only loops.

research_questions.question: Does loop benefit scale with horizon length?
research_questions.falsifiable_answer: Supported if loop advantage grows from short to medium to long tasks.

research_questions.question: Can loops harm performance?
research_questions.falsifiable_answer: Supported if weak-verifier or no-rollback loops regress relative to one-shot baselines.

conditions.name: best_of_n_verifier
conditions.description: Multiple samples selected by an external or calibrated verifier.

conditions.name: self_reflection_loop
conditions.description: Model critiques and revises without external feedback.

conditions.name: grounded_feedback_loop
conditions.description: Model observes tests, tools, or retrieval and revises.

conditions.name: full_state_control_loop
conditions.description: Grounded feedback plus rollback, state ledger, and stopping rule.

conditions.name: weak_verifier_stress
conditions.description: Loop uses intentionally noisy or underpowered verifier.

statistical_models.binary_success: logit(P(success)) ~ condition * horizon_class + feedback_type + log(cost) + (1 | task_family) + (1 | task_id)
statistical_models.continuous_utility: utility ~ condition * horizon_class + feedback_type + log(cost) + (1 | task_family) + (1 | task_id)

predeclared_contrasts.interpretation: Verifier selection matters beyond more samples.

support_criteria: Full loops beat one-shot baselines on long-horizon tasks after cost reporting.
Loop advantage is smaller or absent on short deterministic tasks.
External feedback loops beat self-reflection-only loops.
Weak verifier loops show plateau or regression.
Failure logs show reduced unrepaired error propagation, not merely longer outputs.
weakening_criteria: One-shot baselines match full loops on long-horizon tasks.
Self-reflection-only loops match external feedback loops.
Loop gains vanish after cost normalization.
Failures are dominated by verifier error, memory corruption, or context drift.
Negative controls show loops help equally on trivial tasks.
